analysis.investment_thesis: Anup Engineering is a quality niche player riding India's energy capex super-cycle (LNG, hydrogen, petrochemicals) with 24.5% revenue CAGR and expanding 17.9% operating margins — the business story is real. However, at 4,075 Cr market cap and 34.8x P/E with promoter holding below 50%, this fails three of my non-negotiable entry filters simultaneously; the multibagger math simply doesn't work from here.
key_strengths: Strong revenue compounding — 24.5% CAGR (FY20-25), net profit CAGR 22.4%, operating margins expanding to 17.9%
Secular tailwind from India's energy transition: LNG, hydrogen, fertilizers, defence fabrication — massive multi-decade order pipeline
Conservative balance sheet — D/E 0.25, ROE 18.9%, ROCE 18.3% show capital efficiency on a growing base
key_risks: Valuation is the primary risk — P/E 34.8x and EV/EBITDA 22.4x leave zero margin of safety for a capital-goods cyclical
Promoter holding 40.92% is below my 50% floor — limited skin in the game and signals possible ownership dilution risk
FY25 OCF turned negative (-7 Cr) and FCF is -51 Cr; borrowings jumped to 158 Cr — working capital stress during capex cycle must be watched
red_flags: Market cap 4,075 Cr — more than 2x my upper limit of ~2,000 Cr; institutional discovery already complete
P/E 34.8x vs my sweet spot of 8-15x — paying full price for a cyclical with order-book concentration risk
Promoter at 40.92% — breaches my 50% minimum threshold; no strong promoter conviction signal
FY25 free cash flow -51 Cr despite 733 Cr revenue — profit is not yet converting to cash reliably
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Anup Engineering checks the 'E' (extra-large market) and 'L' (large aspiration) boxes of my SMILE framework convincingly — process equipment for LNG terminals, hydrogen plants, and petrochemical complexes is a 50,000+ Cr addressable market in India alone over the next decade, and Anup's order book reflects this tailwind. The financials are directionally correct: revenue scaled from 245 Cr to 733 Cr in five years, operating margins held at 17-18% through the capex cycle, and the balance sheet remains lightly leveraged. This is a well-run, niche engineering franchise.

The problem is entirely one of entry price and SMILE compliance. At 4,075 Cr market cap, this is firmly a mid-cap — institutional investors (DII 16.1%, FII 4%) have already discovered it, and at P/E 34.8x the multibagger arithmetic is broken. I need to buy a 100-Cr company and ride it to 1,000 Cr; here the market has already priced in perfection. Adding to this, promoter holding at 40.92% is a structural concern — I want the promoter to own more than half the business, not less. Watch this company; if a broad market correction takes it to sub-20x P/E and promoter pledges/holding improve, the calculus changes entirely. Today, patience is the right call.
